Subject: High latency + 429s impacting pipelines — urgent

Sean —

We started seeing a severe spike in end-to-end latency and a steady stream of 429s against your inference endpoints around 09:10 PDT this morning. Our batch ingest queues are backing up and several downstream customers are reporting delayed reports.

What I can tell you so far:
- Requests per second from our integration jumped from ~120 RPS to ~380 RPS between 09:05–09:12.
- We observed repeated 429s and partial responses, not consistent with our usual traffic patterns.
- We attached the request snapshot (request-snapshot-20260818.log) and a short KPI screenshot from our monitoring.

We are on a dedicated plan (customer id VA-1987) and were not expecting throttles. Please triage — this is impacting our SLAs and retention-sensitive workflows.

Emma Chen

emma@valeoanalytics.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High latency + 429s impacting pipelines — urgent

Quick technical notes from the infra side (initial, non-final):

What we see:
- At ~09:10 PDT there are coincident policy triggers: the account-level quota token-bucket and an org-level safety valve both reached threshold.
- The org safety valve policy was recently tightened (rolled 08/17) to clamp shared-pool bursts; combined with Valeo's bursts this created a hysteresis effect where tokens oscillate instead of smoothing.
- The token refill math is correct for single-policy cases, but when two leaky-bucket windows overlap we get intermittent shedding: flows surge, safety valve trips, latency spikes as requests queue, then the shared pool refills slowly — repeat.
- Error profile: majority are 429 + small fraction of 503s as some fallback paths hit saturation.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (we can do now):
1) Temporarily raise Valeo's account quota ceiling by 2x for the next 2 hours to allow the inflight backlog to drain.
2) Push a short rollback of the org safety-valve tightening to the previous threshold (08/16 policy) — this requires Marissa approval for a cross-org policy rollback.
3) Enable a short-lived bypass route to dedicated pool for Valeo traffic (if they accept) to avoid shared pool interference.

I attached token-bucket-debug-0818.csv with per-second token counts for both account and org buckets — it shows the ping-pong pattern starting at 09:09.

I'll stand by to apply changes once we get approvals; if we do nothing the oscillation will continue and we will keep seeing degraded throughput and elevated latency.

-Karthik
Staff Reliability Engineer (on-call)
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: token-bucket-debug-0818.csv)

Emma —

Thanks for the logs. Quick update and immediate actions we just applied:
- Temporarily increased Valeo account quota by 2x (effective now).
- Rolled back the org-level safety valve to the previous threshold as an emergency measure.
- Enabled a targeted routing bypass so your traffic is prioritized to the dedicated pool for the next 90 minutes while your backlog drains.

Early indicators: 30 minutes after the change we see error rate drop ~85% and p95 latency returning toward baseline. Please confirm if your queues are draining on your side.

Next steps we are taking:
- Karthik will open a small hotfix to token-bucket interaction handling to prevent overlapping-window oscillation (ETA: 48 hours).
- We'll schedule an after-action review to discuss whether burst windows should be progressively relaxed for long-tail customers on Dedicated plans.
- If the impact on usage costs is material, we will propose a customer credit; I'll loop in our CS/Finance leads.

We remain available on this thread for any follow-ups.

—Sean
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal summary: Valeo outage root cause & proposed customer relief

Folks —

Summary: Valeo (VA-1987) experienced a customer-impacting surge at 09:10 PDT due to an interaction between a tightened org-level safety valve and the customer's own token-bucket bursts. The overlapping leaky-bucket windows produced flow-control oscillation that manifested as elevated latency and 429s.

Impact: approximately 45 minutes of elevated error rates and 30–60 minute queue backlogs for Valeo. Early telemetry shows error rates fell >80% after rollback + quota raise.

Actions taken: temporary quota increase, emergency rollback of the org safety valve, traffic bypass to dedicated pool. Karthik to ship a correctness hotfix for policy composition within 48 hours.

Recommendation for customer relief: offer one month of service credit and a technical review session led by our platform team. We should also fast-track the hotfix to prevent recurrence.

Please reply with approvals for: 1) policy rollback being made permanent for similar Dedicated customers, and 2) the proposed service credit.

—Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
